note: 2026-10-20 DAILY BATCH, committed under the chairman's hand before any seat was convened. ONE QUESTION, ONE DOCKET. Does ICSID's case-detail page for ICSID Case No. UNCT/20/6 (Einarsson and others v. Canada; NAFTA; UNCITRAL Rules) name, in its own 'Published Decisions' DOCUMENT LIST, any entry corresponding to Procedural Order No. 11 (21 February 2025) or No. 12 (14 March 2025) -- and does that list number its procedural-order entries at all? WHY THIS AND WHY IT IS RE-SPECIFIED: yesterday's close-out (analytics/daily-research/2026-10-19.md section 5.7 item 1) named a body-region row on this document list as today's cheapest business, on the stated ground that POs 11 and 12 are 'named by designation and date and unread' while the numbered run in the held 2026-08-18/08-19 windows ends at No. 10, so whether 11 and 12 'appear later in that list is unobserved'. I RE-SPECIFY THAT QUESTION, and the reason is a property of this instrument rather than of the docket: a NUMBERED find cannot answer it. excerpt_of returns the FIRST occurrence only (scripts/fetch_relay.py:128-133), and every 'Procedural Order No. N' literal occurs in the page's CHRONOLOGY region before it could occur in the document list -- which is exactly what yesterday's own row A4 demonstrated: the find 'Procedural Order No. 11' returned the chronology window 'February 21, 2025 The Tribunal issues Procedural Order No. 11 concerning the organization of the hearing.  March 3, 2025 - March 13, 2025 The Tribunal holds a hearing on jurisdiction and the merits in person in Calgary and by video conference. March 14, 2025 The Tribunal issues Procedural Order No. 12 concerning procedural matters.' That row observed the chronology and NOT the list, and no numbered find on this page ever can. The list must therefore be walked with LIST-REGION anchors, which is what rows 3 and 4 do. WHAT THIS COUNCIL ALREADY HOLDS ON THE LIST, re-derived in session from the result files themselves over all 705 rows in 93 analytics/fetch-results/*.json files and not taken from any note: ONE prior 'Published Decisions' row exists on this URL (2026-09-03, analytics/fetch-results/2026-09-03-daily2.json, find_matched TRUE, status 200) and its window reads '(a) Original Proceeding Published Decisions Witness Statement of Theodore David Einarsson (Public Version) Procedural Order Statement of Defence Confidentiality Order Witness Statement of Russell John Einarsson (Public Version) Witness Statement of Ralph Maitland Expert Report of Nigel Bankes Expert Report of “Chip” Gordon'. THE LIST'S ONLY PROCEDURAL-ORDER ENTRY IN ANY HELD WINDOW IS THE BARE, UNNUMBERED STRING 'Procedural Order'. That is the observation this batch tests and extends, and it is already enough to show that yesterday's 'numbered run ends at No. 10' premise describes the chronology, not this list. PRIOR ART ON THIS URL, re-derived in session and CORRECTED BEFORE THIS BATCH WAS PUSHED (my first draft of this note said '37 rows across 15 dates' and that figure was wrong): 25 rows across 8 dates -- 2026-08-13 (1), 2026-08-26 (2), 2026-09-03 (4), 2026-09-04 (2), 2026-09-05 (3), 2026-09-06 (2), 2026-09-07 (6), 2026-10-19 (5). THE DATES ARE RESULT-FILE DATES AND NOT ROW TIMESTAMPS, because all 25 rows carry NO per-row timestamp field -- the only time any result file records is the batch-level 'fetched_at' -- so 'dates observed' can only mean distinct result files' dates and is stated that way rather than implying a precision the records do not hold. Last observed YESTERDAY, so this is a one-day re-observation justified by the list question and not by any cadence. PER-FIND COUNTS CORPUS-WIDE: 'Status of Proceeding' 70 fired / 70 TRUE (12 / 12 on this URL); 'Published Decisions' 11 fired / 7 TRUE (1 / 1 on this URL); 'Procedural Order Statement of Defence' 0 fired; 'Expert Report of Nigel Bankes' 0 fired. FOUR ROWS, ONE URL, within MAX_URLS = 12 (scripts/fetch_relay.py:76). The control https://example.com/ is prepended by the relay itself and is not written below; if it fails the batch is VOID and no row may be read as information about this docket. Host icsid.worldbank.org is on ALLOWED_HOSTS (scripts/fetch_relay.py:48). The UNENCODED 'CaseNo=' form is used: certified 200 by all prior unencoded rows on this URL. COMPANION CONTROLS: rows 3 and 4 may null, and their companion controls are ROWS 1 AND 2 ON THE SAME URL IN THE SAME RUN, as analytics/fetch-requests/README.md requires -- when a find misses, excerpt_of returns the empty string rather than a head excerpt (:132-133), so a null row hands back no window and is uninterpretable alone. THE BASELINE THE MOVEMENT ROW IS READ AGAINST: 'Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: December 16, 2025 - Each party files a reply statement of costs.' observed YESTERDAY. It is itself an advance on the 'December 2, 2025 - Each party files a statement of costs.' span that was character-identical across twelve rows on nine dates from 2026-08-13 to 2026-09-07. DIFF ON THE PROSE, NEVER ON sha256 OR bytes: this URL holds twelve distinct sha256 values across nine dates on a page whose watched span never changed by one character. A DIFFERING DIGEST OR BYTE COUNT IS NOT MOVEMENT and may never be written as movement. WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS: a disposition, a holding, a ground, or any statement about what any tribunal decided. G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition; G10 bars reading a document DESIGNATION as a tribunal's characterisation -- so 'Procedural Order No. 11 concerning the organization of the hearing' and a hearing recorded as 'on jurisdiction and the merits' support ONLY that the docket so records them, never that the tribunal bifurcated, joined, or decided anything. A list entry's presence supports ONLY that a document so titled is named as published; its contents remain wholly unread by this council. An ABSENCE in the list supports ONLY that the list does not name such an entry in the retrieved window -- never that no such procedural order issued, and never that it is unpublished. RING STATUS, STATED SO NO SUCCESSOR INFLATES IT: on this council's own held reduction the covered investment on UNCT/20/6 is recorded as a 'Seismic data enterprise' under NAFTA. THAT IS A DATA-ASSET DESIGNATION ON A DOCKET-SUMMARY FIELD AND IT IS NOT AN ESTABLISHED RING-1 PLEADING -- no patent, trademark, GI, trade secret or clinical-trial data is pleaded as the covered investment on any body this council has retrieved, and nothing in this batch can establish one. OUTCOME CLASSES THAT ARE FACTS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT AND MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN AS FINDINGS ABOUT ICSID OR ABOUT THIS MATTER: control_ok false (whole batch VOID); refused / 403 / 202 / timeout / no_contact; host_not_allowed / scheme_not_https; and a 404 OR A REDIRECT, which is never a statement that a case does not exist -- it would mean only that this designator does not resolve on this surface at this instant, and the project's absence rule is 'not found in accessible sources'. CADENCE AND SCOPE: this batch touches and re-anchors NOTHING ELSE. It is NOT thread 11's search limb (due on or around 2026-10-25, deliberately not pulled forward); it is NOT thread 11's relay row into the Decisions on Manifest Lack of Legal Merit register; it is NOT locked-set row 1-02's forum row; it is NOT the monthly watch on threads 10 or 25; it does NOT touch ARB/22/2 (monthly, next due 2026-11-18), ARB/17/19 (observed yesterday) or ARB/12/1. urls.purpose: ROW 1 -- THE CERTIFIED ANCHOR AND THE MOVEMENT ROW, and the first companion control for rows 3 and 4. Expected HIT (70 fired / 70 TRUE corpus-wide; 12 / 12 on this URL). The window carries both watched fields in one span and yesterday's reading was 'Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: December 16, 2025 - Each party files a reply statement of costs.' A CHARACTER-IDENTICAL RETURN IS THE NULL ON MOVEMENT and is this row's expected outcome one day on. A CHANGED Status -- in particular 'Concluded' with an 'Outcome of Proceeding' line in place of 'Latest Development' -- or a later development date is reported as a DOCKET-SUMMARY FIELD and never as a disposition. This row also reaches the head of the document list in its right context, which is how the 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-19 windows overlap and is what lets row 2's span be checked for character-level stability.

ROW 2 -- THE LIST-HEAD ROW and the second companion control. Expected HIT (11 fired / 7 TRUE corpus-wide; 1 / 1 on this URL, 2026-09-03). Its purpose is to re-observe the one held list window on this URL for character-level stability after 47 days: '(a) Original Proceeding Published Decisions Witness Statement of Theodore David Einarsson (Public Version) Procedural Order Statement of Defence Confidentiality Order Witness Statement of Russell John Einarsson (Public Version) Witness Statement of Ralph Maitland Expert Report of Nigel Bankes Expert Report of “Chip” Gordon'. A NEW ENTRY APPEARING AT THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, or a changed order, is the cheapest signal available that the published-document set has grown since costs submissions closed. A character-identical return is the null on publication and is the expected outcome.

ROW 3 -- THE LIST-REGION DISCRIMINATOR, and the row this batch exists for. First firing of this literal anywhere in the corpus (0 fired). It is the only row in this batch that can reach the document list WITHOUT reaching the chronology first, because the chronology's procedural-order sentences always read 'Procedural Order No. N concerning ...' and never place the bare string 'Procedural Order' immediately before 'Statement of Defence'. A HIT therefore establishes, at character level, that this list's procedural-order entry is BARE AND UNNUMBERED and that no numbered entry sits in that position -- which is the direct answer to whether the list numbers its procedural orders at all, and it is the premise yesterday's next-step wording got wrong by reading a chronology property as a list property. A FALSE supports ONLY that this exact adjacency is not present in the retrieved window: it would mean the list's composition has changed or that the two entries are no longer adjacent, and it would NOT mean any procedural order is unpublished. Companion controls are rows 1 and 2 on the same URL in the same run.

ROW 4 -- THE DEEPEST REACH THIS COUNCIL HAS EVER TAKEN INTO THIS LIST. First firing of this literal anywhere in the corpus (0 fired). Every find anchor sits at offset 100 of its own 400-character window (scripts/fetch_relay.py:134-135, EXCERPT_CHARS = 400), so this row returns roughly 300 characters to the right of an entry that sits within 30 characters of the END of the one held list window on this URL -- a reach of about 290 characters of list text this council has never seen. THE GAIN IS STATED AS AN ESTIMATE AND NOT AS A MEASUREMENT, because the exact offset of this anchor in the live body is unobserved. Expected HIT if the 2026-09-03 list order holds. What it is FOR: if the list continues past the expert reports into hearing-stage or decision-stage documents, that is where any entry corresponding to Procedural Order No. 11 or No. 12 -- or to the March 2025 hearing on jurisdiction and the merits -- would be named. A FALSE supports ONLY that this entry is not present in the retrieved window, which would itself be a change in the list and would be reported as one. No designation retrieved by this row may be written as a holding, a ground or a disposition (G10, G16). Companion controls are rows 1 and 2 on the same URL in the same run.
